messages:
alex: Hey — running into intermittent JSONDecodeError in our Python client when consuming the hosted SSE stream. It only happens under load. Trace looks like:
```
  File "/app/stream_consumer.py", line 42, in _handle_chunk
    obj = json.loads(buf)
json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
```
I think chunks are splitting JSON objects across events. Using `requests` with `stream=True` + `iter_lines()` and then stripping leading `data:`. Anyone seen this and have robust parsers/patterns?

priya: Yep, classic partial-JSON issue. If the server can guarantee each SSE event contains a complete JSON object that's ideal (one object per event). If not, you need to reassemble. Quick pattern using JSONDecoder.raw_decode to greedily parse prefixes from a buffer:
```
buf += chunk
dec = json.JSONDecoder()
while buf:
    try:
        obj, idx = dec.raw_decode(buf)
        process(obj)
        buf = buf[idx:].lstrip()
    except ValueError:
        # incomplete, wait for more
        break
```
This avoids counting braces (which breaks on strings). Use this with `iter_content(chunk_size=None)` rather than `iter_lines()` if you need exact bytes.

sara: Also check your SSE framing: the SSE spec allows multiple `data:` lines per event. Many server frameworks send JSON across several `data:` lines, so your per-event assembly should join all `data:` lines until the blank line `\n\n`. Example assembly: collect lines that start with `data:` and join with `\n` then parse the joined string. If the server is the one splitting a single JSON onto multiple `data:` lines, you still get a complete JSON per event after join. If the server is splitting events mid-object (i.e., sending half an event then later continuing the rest as a new event), that's a server bug and should be fixed.

mike: For backpressure under load, decouple network read from processing. In asyncio: push parsed events into an asyncio.Queue with a bounded size. If the queue is full, pause reading from the HTTP response (flow-control) or apply backpressure to the producer. With `aiohttp` you can control how much you read: `await resp.content.read(n)` and await when queue has room. Example sketch:
```
queue = asyncio.Queue(maxsize=200)
async for chunk in resp.content.iter_chunked(4096):
    buf += chunk.decode()
    for obj in try_extract(buf):
        await queue.put(obj)  # blocks when full -> backpressure
    # consumer pulls from queue and processes
```
In Node, you can `req.pause()`/`req.resume()` on an incoming stream if processing lags. In plain threads, use a bounded queue that blocks producers.

priya: If you can't rely on braces correctness or event boundaries, consider a streaming JSON parser: `ijson` (Python) or `clarinet`/`JSONStream` (Node) which can parse incremental JSON reliably. For SSE where each event is supposed to be an object, `raw_decode` is often enough and avoids pulling in a heavy dependency.

alex: Nice, thanks. A couple follow-ups: 1) we're currently stripping `data:` lines and feeding the remainder into the buffer; we might be losing the per-event newline join semantics — will switch to reassembling multi-line `data:`. 2) any tips about `retry`/reconnect behaviour? We saw clients reconnecting too fast under failure storms.

sara: For reconnect storms, use SSE `retry:` field (ms) sent by server to suggest client backoff, but many clients ignore it. Implement exponential backoff with jitter on the client side (start with server-recommended value if present). Also limit simultaneous reconnects site-wide (circuit-breaker).

mike: Also instrument an internal metric for "parsing backlog" (queue length) and for "avg time to parse" — that'll help tune queue sizes and chunk sizes. If you're using our hosted runtime, we can also add a server-side switch to prefer sending complete JSON-per-event or NDJSON (Content-Type: application/x-ndjson) which simplifies clients.

alex: Good plan. One micro-question — is NDJSON preferable to SSE+JSON for long-lived streams?

priya: NDJSON is simpler if you only need newline-delimited objects and want simpler parsing/rewind semantics. SSE gives you event semantics (`event:`/`id:`/`retry:`) which are handy for reconnection/ordering. If you control both client and server, either works; NDJSON is more firewall/proxy friendly sometimes.

ops-bot: automatic note: deployed a hotfix to staging that ensures server will not split a single JSON object across separate SSE events. Patch id: deploy-2026-03-17-42 :rocket:

alex: Awesome — I'll switch the client to: reassemble `data:` lines per event, feed into JSONDecoder.raw_decode loop, and add bounded queue for backpressure + exponential reconnect jitter. Will report back after verifying in staging. Thanks all :pray:
